Relay the commit program's ledger-revert notice in the emulator harness

Midgard Node CI failed on 15f60017f in
tests/deposit-flow-emulator-merge-payout.test.ts, "runs deposit, reserve
absorption, withdrawal commitment, and payout to conclusion": after the
withdrawal block rejected two transactions at commit, the validation cache
still held their outputs and lacked the input the revert restored
(tests/helpers/production-lifecycle.ts:307, the cache compared with the
spendable ledger).

A commit-stage rejection tells the cache which rows it changed through the
worker's MempoolLedgerRevertedNotice, which the parent turns into stale
marks. The emulator harness runs the commit program in process and passed
it no notifier, so the notice was never posted and nothing else names those
rows: the block that lands includes neither transaction, so the rebase's
keys do not cover them. The comparison in the lifecycle helper and the
stale marks both arrived with the validation-cache commits, and this suite
was not among the ones rerun for them.

The harness's production path now passes a notifier that hands a
MempoolLedgerRevertedNotice to the parent's dispatcher
(takeCommitWorkerOutput), so the same code marks the keys as in the node.
The other notices feed readiness, which the fixture does not follow, and
are not relayed. No source change: the node's worker already posts the
notice and its parent already marks the keys
(tests/mempool-ledger-cache.stale-marks.ts,
tests/commit-worker-reverted-notice.test.ts).

Verified (rerun here):
- Red before, same command:
  node scripts/contrib.mjs test --package midgard-node --file tests/deposit-flow-emulator-merge-payout.test.ts
  failed (2 passed, 1 failed) with the CI assertion at
  tests/helpers/production-lifecycle.ts:307.
- Green after: 3 passed in 1 file.
- Typecheck of midgard-node; eslint --max-warnings=0 and prettier on the
  two files.

Not verified:
- Which of the validation-cache commits first made the case red.
- The other emulator suites on this harness were not rerun here; the change
  acts only when a commit rejects a transaction after admission, which no
  other suite on the production path does. CI runs them all.

Reload the validation cache when a rolled-back deposit is admitted again

A deposit an own landed block includes stays assigned to that block's
header when the follower rewinds past its L1 admission. Its output leaves
the spendable ledger, and the rewind's full reload drops it from the
validation cache. When a later L1 block admitted the deposit again, the
driver saw an advance with no orphans to settle and no mempool row to
restore, so nothing told the cache to read the output again: a spend of it
was rejected as a missing input until the next full reload. A deposit a
foreign landed block includes was not affected (its orphan keeps the write
gate pending, and clearing it recomputes).

reconcileFollowerEvents now also reports the working-ledger outrefs of
header-assigned deposits whose admission entered the chain after the view
it last ingested (l1_event_keys.first_canonical_slot above
follower_event_ingestion.slot), read before the ingestion point moves. They
travel with the restored rows as `spendableRestored` (outrefs; it replaces
`spendableUpserts`), so the advance raises the recompute for them and the
keyed repair names them, as both already did for restored rows.

The regression case is in tests/follower-tick.test.ts, over the production
driver, sink and recompute on a real follower store and one validation
cache: the deposit's output is spent (accepted), the chain rolls back one
block (the spend is rejected E_INPUT_NOT_FOUND), the next block admits the
deposit again and the spend must be accepted. The helper
testDriverRecomputeOverCache leaves the cache layer to the caller so the
test reads the cache the recompute repairs.

Verified (rerun here):
- Red before the fix, same command:
  node scripts/contrib.mjs test --package midgard-node --file tests/follower-tick.test.ts
  failed (1 passed, 1 failed) at the last spend: expected
  { accepted: 1, rejected: [] }, got
  { accepted: 0, rejected: [ 'E_INPUT_NOT_FOUND' ] }; the re-admission run
  before it was an applied advance with no holds.
- Green after: 2 passed in 1 file.
- Suites the change reaches, by file: 74 passed in 12 files
  (follower-tick, follower-driver-recompute, follower-events-ingestion,
  follower-events-refusals, own-block-event-orphaned, six landed-blocks

  (deposit-flow-emulator-commit-selection, l2-peer-scheduler-emulator).
- Typecheck: midgard-node, midgard-watcher, midgard-node-tools,
  midgard-fault-proofs. eslint --max-warnings=0 and prettier on the six
  files; "Verified 215 module-size ceilings."
- spendableUpserts has no remaining reference under demo/.

Not verified:

Mark stale keys for the validation cache instead of logging deltas

Writers of `mempool_ledger` outside the validation cache told it what
changed through a versioned delta ring. Production published only
full-reload markers on it, so every outside write cost the cache a
whole-table load, and the ring needed a size limit
(VALIDATION_LEDGER_DELTA_LOG_MAX).

The ring is replaced by stale marks, `MEMPOOL_LEDGER_STALE: { all,
keys }`. A writer marks the keys it changed once its write has
committed (`markMempoolLedgerStale`), or every key when it cannot name
them. The cache takes the marks when it synchronizes and reads those
keys again, or loads in full when every key is marked, and repeats
until no mark arrived during its read. A failed read puts its marks
back. The spendable view cannot tell at a marked key or one being read
again, and anywhere while every key is marked or a full load runs.

- The commit worker's revert notice now carries the out-refs the
  commit-stage rejection deleted or inserted
  (`MempoolLedgerRevertedNotice.outRefs`), built and parsed in the
  shared boundary module `workers/utils/commit-block-header.ts`; the
  parent marks exactly those keys. A notice whose payload it cannot
  read marks every key.
  `revertCommitStageRejectedLedgerEffects` returns those out-refs.
- A failed commit attempt, and a worker error with no output, still
  mark every key: which rows a committed revert changed is unknown.
- A keyed read that failed in a poisoned-epoch or canonical recovery
  used to lose its keys; they are marked stale again.
- Deleted with no replacement: the delta log and its ring,
  `publishMempoolLedgerDelta`, `publishFullMempoolLedgerReload`, the
  journal overlay in the spendable view, the delta-apply counter
  (`validation_ledger_cache_delta_apply_count`),
  `SuccessfulSubmissionOutput.mempoolLedgerDeletedOutRefHexes`, and the
  configuration key VALIDATION_LEDGER_DELTA_LOG_MAX.

Not built: a keyed repair for a follower recompute with no orphans.
It rests on every spendability change of such an ingestion being named
in its spendable upserts or rebase keys, and that does not hold: a
header-assigned deposit's row becomes spendable or unspendable with
its follower admission alone, which no ingestion result names.

Tests:
- tests/mempool-ledger-cache.stale-marks.ts (new, in
  tests/mempool-ledger-cache.test.ts): a key marked during the full
  load is read again; every key marked during a load loads again; a
  marked key is read with no full load; a failed read leaves its marks;
  the spendable view at marked keys and during reads; which worker
  outputs mark; a revert notice has exactly its out-refs read again;
  seven malformed notice payloads mark every key.
- tests/commit-worker-reverted-notice.test.ts (new, compiled): the
  notice crosses from the compiled worker codec to the compiled
  dispatcher with its out-refs, and malformed payloads mark every key.

Behaviour to know:
- a key marked stale is answered "cannot tell" until the cache's next
  synchronization reads it; admission then falls back to its own read.
- a keyed read with no keys is skipped.
- the cache still loads `mempool_ledger` in full at process start and
  wherever a writer cannot name its keys (a follower recompute, a failed
  commit attempt, a worker error, an unreadable notice).

- contrib boundary --package midgard-node: passed; contrib gate

- typecheck of midgard-node, midgard-fault-proofs, midgard-watcher and

Read again the keys of patches a keyed canonical recovery drops

A canonical recovery that names the keys its repair changed set the
cache at those keys and dropped every unpromoted patch without reading
the dropped patches' keys again. A patch whose persistence committed
while the retirement stopped its promotion then left the cache with the
pre-patch answers at its keys (a spent input still spendable, a
produced output missing) until the next full load.

The recovery now reads the dropped patches' keys again from
`mempool_ledger`, as the poisoned-epoch recovery already does.

Test (added to the canonical history cache retirement cases of
tests/mempool-ledger-cache.test.ts): a persistence that commits while a
keyed recovery retires its epoch; the cache must answer the committed
rows with no full reload, and the keyed read must be asked for exactly
the patch's keys.

From the implementer's runs, not rerun at this commit:
- before the fix the test failed: the cache held the spent input and
  not the produced output; after the fix it passed.

Verified (rerun here) at the following commit, which rewrites these
lines: the test passes there.

Build validation-trace defense material on the store ledger

The defense material build loaded all of `confirmed_ledger`, replayed
the landed chain over it in memory and passed the whole predecessor
ledger to its worker thread. It now takes the ledger at the disputed
block's parent from the node's ledger store by its root (rebuilt from
the newest retained ledger on the chain to the parent when the store
no longer holds that root), keeps it on the main thread, and serves
the worker's reads over a message channel of its own
(`validation-trace-defense/ledger-port.ts`): trie nodes by hash and
outputs by out-ref. A build reads only what the event's replay
touches.

- The block's retained DA payload is looked up before any ledger work:
  a case whose payload is missing reads no ledger.
- Every failure to get or read the parent ledger makes the case
  `unavailable`, which is retried at the next tick and never cached.
- The owner-store lookup landed-block processing uses is now one
  function, `ownerRetainedLedger`, shared with the defense fiber.
- `landedLedger`, `applyDelta` and `LedgerMap` in
  `landed-blocks/ledger.ts` have no caller left in `src`.

Tests:
- tests/validation-trace-defense-ledger-port.test.ts (new, no
  emulator): the build over the channel gives the fault-proofs
  builder's material byte for byte at four step counts, and the
  operator's fault on a failing block; a predecessor 256 times larger
  serves the same outputs and at most two more trie levels per touched
  key; a served read failing at any one read gives `unavailable` or the
  reference material, never another verdict; the worker side gets each
  output as a `Buffer`.
- tests/validation-trace-defense-survey-emulator.test.ts (three
  added): no ledger lookup and no ledger row read for a case with no
  retained payload; `unavailable` and nothing cached while the store
  cannot give the parent ledger, then an answer once it can; the same
  material from a store that retains only the frontier's ledger.

Verified (rerun here):
- contrib test midgard-node, survey, fiber, max-shape, restart and
  end-to-end emulator suites with the port test: 25 passed in 6 files,
  exit 0.
- contrib test midgard-node, race, replacement, funding and references
  emulator suites: 14 passed in 4 files.
- tests/landed-blocks-rebase-keyed-io.test.ts: 1 passed, exit 0.
- Each guard weakened by a temporary edit, then restored: an output
  left a plain Uint8Array (the Buffer test fails), a build failure
  reported as an operator fault (the fault sweep fails), a store
  failure reported as an operator fault, the ledger looked up before
  the payload, and an empty lineage (one survey test fails for each).
- Typecheck of midgard-node, midgard-fault-proofs, midgard-watcher and
  midgard-node-tools; eslint, prettier and the module-size check.

From the implementer's runs, not rerun:
- contrib boundary --package midgard-node and contrib gate
  process-boundaries passed; the gate does not include the defense
  material worker.
- A rejected read resolved as an empty answer makes the fault sweep
  fail.
- Trie nodes read by one build: 12 at 16 predecessor entries, 74 at
  4,096. The consensus-maximum build's Defend tick took 6,669 ms.

Not verified:
- One earlier survey-suite run had the frontier-only case answer
  `unavailable` while another process rebuilt the native owner binary
  under it; it passed in every run since (four here), and its cause
  was not captured.
- The emulator suites ran with
  MIDGARD_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=preprod-emulator-testing set by hand.

- The emulator suites ran with
  MIDGARD_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=preprod-emulator-testing set by hand.

Expose the node and output source a store ledger reads

`ledgerReads(ledger)` gives the source a ledger store ledger reads its
trie nodes and outputs from, its overlay first and then its store. A
reader that cannot hold the ledger itself (a worker thread served over
a message port) reads as the ledger does through
`ledgerAt(ledger.root, ledgerReads(ledger))`. A `Ledger` that is not a
ledger store ledger is refused.

The validation-trace defender scene's test support also exports the
one-event Plutus block fixture and the predecessor filler, for builds
outside the emulator.

Tests (two added to tests/ledger-store.read.test.ts):
- under `ledgerAt`, the source of a store ledger, and of one with an
  applied overlay, gives that ledger's reads, proofs and root;
- a ledger that is not a ledger store ledger is refused.

Verified (rerun here):
- contrib test @al-ft/midgard-fault-proofs --file
  tests/ledger-store.read.test.ts: 10 passed in 1 file, exit 0.
- midgard-fault-proofs typecheck.

From the implementer's runs, not rerun:
- with the refusal removed, "refuses a ledger that is not a ledger
  store ledger" fails.

Keep the validation cache's working ledger once, and repair it at keys

The cache held the working ledger in memory twice: the durable entries,
and a second map with the unpromoted Phase B patches applied. After
every landed-block rebase it cleared the second map and copied every
durable entry into it again. A poisoned pipeline epoch reloaded all of
mempool_ledger.

- One in-memory ledger (mempool-ledger-cache.working-ledger.ts): the
  durable entries, with the unpromoted patches looked up over them,
  newest first. Nothing is copied. currentState and the spendable view
  answer through that lookup; MempoolLedgerState is the lookup type.
- applyPatchAndSync, which nothing in src called, is gone.
- A poisoned epoch drops the unpromoted patches and reads again only the
  keys they named. Each persistence commits its ledger rows in one
  transaction (txAdmissions.mark-accepted.ts) at keys its patch names,
  and recovery waits for earlier persistence under the persistence lock,
  so the durable entries can differ from the table only at those keys.
- spendableAt moves from the follower repair into MempoolLedgerDB, and
  the cache takes it as its keyed read.
- New counter validation_ledger_cache_entry_write_count: entries written
  into the in-memory ledger by full loads, deltas, keyed repairs and
  promotions.

The cache still loads the whole working ledger at process start and
wherever the changed keys are unknown.

Tests (tests/mempool-ledger-cache.working-ledger.ts, run from
mempool-ledger-cache.test.ts):
- A keyed recovery and a promotion over 2,000 loaded rows move the
  counter by 3 and 2: red if a copy of the ledger comes back.
- 80 seeded random steps of patches, promotions, cancels, keyed and full
  recoveries: every key answers as a cache loaded from scratch does.
- A poisoned recovery asks the keyed read for exactly the patch keys,
  the full-reload count does not move, and a persistence that committed
  before its promotion was interrupted is found.
The tests that walked the cache's map now compare lookups at the keys
they wrote.

Verified (rerun here): 51 passed in 6 files (mempool-ledger-cache,
own-block-event-orphaned, landed-blocks-rebase-keyed-io,
admission-input-claims, listen-router.tx-evaluate,
follower-driver-recompute); midgard-node typecheck.

From the implementer's runs, not rerun: each guard killed once (a full
copy in repair and in promote, repair or promote skipping deletes or
upserts, a poisoned recovery that reloads in full, re-reads without
repairing, asks for one key fewer or leaves out deletes: every one
failed a test); deposit-flow-emulator-submission and
commit-parent-lease-emulator (2 passed); the database suite's submit
latency case (1 passed); typechecks of midgard-watcher,
midgard-fault-proofs and midgard-node-tools; eslint, prettier and the
module-size check.

Not verified: wall-clock or memory before and after; the benchmark was
edited and typechecks but was not run; no test poisons an epoch through
the production construction of the cache.
